name: Lechon Kawali (Filipino Crispy Fried Pork Belly)

ingredients.name: boneless skin-on pork belly, cut in half

instructions.primary_message: In a large pot, place pork belly skin side down and add enough water to completely submerge meat. Add garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, and soy sauce. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then lower heat and reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook until pork skin can be pierced with a knife with no resistance, about 1 hour. Transfer pork to a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet and season liberally with salt all over. Refrigerate pork until skin has completely dried, 6 hours or overnight.
Remove pork from refrigerator and cut into 2-inch slices.

Fill a wok or Dutch oven with at least 4 inches oil and heat to 375°F over high heat. Working in batches, fry pork until deeply browned and skin has bubbled and crisped, 7 to 10 minutes. Transfer pork to a paper towel-lined plate and season with salt to taste. Cut pork slices into 1-inch pieces. Serve immediately with vinegar or Lechon sauce for dipping.

description: Filipino lechon kawali is one of the great pork dishes of the world. Boiled pork belly gets fried until intensely crisp and crunchy on the outside and meltingly tender within.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 7 hr 45 min.

Optional or for serving: Rice or cane vinegar, preferably spicy, or Lechon sauce (such as Mang Tomas), for dipping

Optional substitutions: Canola oil → peanut oil
author: Joshua Bousel
